Mark Richard Hopking (Born 28 April 1971)is a British mariner and superyacht captain.  His career includes serving as captain during two Antarctic seasons of the environmental expedition yacht 2041 and later commanding the 78-metre motor yacht Hampshire II. He subsequently acted as Project Manager and Build Captain for the 74-metre Feadship yacht Sherpa, a project followed in a documentary in which he featured. Hopking's work has also appeared in earlier documentaries, including a 1993 ITV film about a Cape Horn expedition and Channel 4's Cutting Edge series. He holds the Scottish feudal barony of Balvill and is a fellow to the Society of Antiquaries of Scotland.
Maritime Career
Hopking’s maritime career began in the early 1990's at the John Ridgway Adventure School in Sutherland, Scotland. He served as crew aboard the English Rose VI, a yacht which previously competed in the 1977–78 Whitbread Round the World Race under the name Debenhams.
During the 1990s, he joined Rebecca Ridgway's kayaking expedition around Cape Horn. The expedition was documented in a 1993 ITV film and Ridgway's book Something Amazing, both which illustrate Hopking's involvement. He also appeared in "Exposure", a 1993 episode of Channel 4’s Cutting Edge documentary series.
In 1998, a Daily Telegraph feature profiled his career and financial planning related to his work with The Challenge Business, organisers of the Global Challenge race.
In 1999, Hopking became captain of the yacht 2041, acquired by environmentalist Robert Swan for an Antarctic Treaty awareness programme. He skippered the vessel from the United Kingdom to the Antarctic Peninsula. The voyage and expeditions were documented in the book, 2041: Voyage South.
Hopking moved into the superyacht sector in 2001, later commanding the 78-metre motor yacht Hampshire II between 2011 and 2016. In this capacity, he contributed to matters of document control, for which he was awarded, and public discussion on regulatory pressures. and changes within the superyacht sector.
He subsequently served as project manager and build captain for the 74-metre Feadship yacht [https://www.feadship.nl/fleet/sherpa Sherpa], overseeing construction at Feadship's Royal Van Lent shipyard. The build process was documented in industry profiles and a documentary in which Hopking appeared.
Barony of Balvill
Debrett's lists Hopking as the current holder of the feudal Barony of Balvill. A dignity created by Crown charter in 1630 which continued as incorporeal heritable property following the Abolition of Feudal Tenure etc. (Scotland) Act 2000.
Heraldry
Hopking was granted arms by the Court of the Lord Lyon in 2018. A further matriculation in 2026 granted
Tartan
Hopking holds a personal tartan within the Scottish Register of Tartans.
Personal Life
Hopking maintains an active interest in Scottish heraldry and genealogy, through which he gained fellowship in the Society of Antiquaries of Scotland.
